text: sam: quick accessibility pass notes on the Model > Performance sparklines — found two separate problems: (1) keyboard navigation jumps into the chart canvas before the legend chips when using Tab/Shift+Tab, and (2) the legend swatch colors fail contrast when the user enables the high-contrast toggle. sam: repro (short): ``` 1) Console > Models > select a model > Performance tab 2) enable high-contrast mode in profile settings 3) tab into the sparklines panel and use Tab / Shift+Tab 4) focus lands on the chart canvas (tabindex=0) then the chips, even though visually the chips are above the chart ``` zoe: saw this on VoiceOver too. Screen reader announces the chart first because the canvas is earlier in DOM order. Legend is purely visual so VO doesn't create a strong association. harper: small DOM and ARIA fixes would make this reliable: keep logical DOM order matching visual flow (legend before canvas) OR add aria-describedby on the chart pointing at the legend container id so assistive tech ties them together. amar: adding to that ensure each legend chip uses role=\"button\" (not just div) and aria-pressed to reflect selection state. That helps keyboard + SR announce state changes. chai: contrast suggestion: the current teal swatch (#5EEAD4) fails against light and high-contrast backgrounds. propose token swap: --sparkline-1: #059669 (emerald-600) and --sparkline-2: #2563EB (indigo-600) for stronger strokes. I'll attach WCAG 2.1 AA checks. sam: screen reader messaging: when a chip toggles visibility, emit a polite aria-live region update like \"Legend: Latency hidden\". Keeps SR users in the loop without disturbing focus. harper: also fallback text for svg charts: include and <desc> children and ensure IDs are referenced by aria-labelledby on the svg. Some assistive tech prefers labelled svg content over generic role=\"img\". sam: example snippets: ```html <div id=\"perf-legend\" aria-label=\"performance metric legend\"> <button class=\"legend-chip\" role=\"button\" aria-pressed=\"false\">Latency</button> <button class=\"legend-chip\" role=\"button\" aria-pressed=\"true\">Throughput</button> </div> <svg role=\"img\" aria-labelledby=\"chart-title chart-desc\" tabindex=\"0\"> <title id=\"chart-title\">Model latency chart Sparkline for latency and throughput; legend: references the chips above. ``` chai: CSS focus polish for high-contrast mode: ```css .legend-chip:focus { outline: 3px solid var(--focus-ring); } .sparkline path { stroke-width: 2px; } ``` amar: testing notes: update e2e to Tab through the panel (assert DOM order) and add axe-core rule for color-contrast on the legend swatches. Add a small VoiceOver manual step in the issue checklist: verify announcement order and aria-live updates. sam: opened issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/issues/4387 with screenshots, color contrast proofs, and a tiny recording. tagging 1.19 for full fix; contrast token swap considered low-risk and could land in 1.18.3 if design signoff quick. harper: quick follow-up if we keep the canvas tabbable for keyboard pan/zoom, we should add aria-describedby to the canvas referencing the legend and control hints (e.g., \"Use arrow keys to pan, +/- to zoom\"). deploy-bot: scheduled canary deploy for branch \"fix/perf-sparklines-a11y-4387\" to staging in 15 minutes. sam: thanks all I'll attach the PR with the DOM reorder + aria updates and ping for reviews. zoe: I'll QA VoiceOver + NVDA after staging canary lands.
